The Philippines on Thursday said it has filed a diplomatic protest against China for its dangerous maneuvers that caused significant damage to one of its vessels and injury to a Filipino crew during an incident at Scarborough Shoal.

No further details were provided, but the Department of Foreign Affairs said a note verbale was sent to China on Thursday.

The Philippine government condemned what it called "illegal and hostile actions" by the China Coast Guard Aquatic Resources ship and Chinese Maritime Millia vessels against the Philippines' Bureau of Fisheries ship during a humanitarian mission for Filipino fishermen on Sept. 16 near Scarborough Shoal, called Bajo de Masinloc by Manila and Huangyan Island by Beijing.

https://t.co/n0ihrsTNZW

Traffic Advisory

18 September 2025

ROAD CLOSURE ON SOWETO HIGHWAY IN DIEPKLOOF DUE TO SHOOTING INCIDENT

The Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department can confirm a fatal shooting incident on Soweto Highway in Diepkloof with both directions on the route being blocked off to traffic between the N1 and Immink Drive.

It is understood that a taxi boss has been fatally shot. 

Emergency personnel and Law Enforcement officials are currently on the scene. 

Motorists are advised to exercise patience and caution and to avoid the route as vehicles are being diverted at the N1 and Immink Drive. 

-END-

Issued by the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department Communication Unit #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic #SaferJoburg #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje

Caritas Philippines president Bishop Jose Colin Bagaforo said the proceedings will begin at the Luneta or Rizal Park in Manila at 9 a.m. which will culminate at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City in the afternoon.

LOOK: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Thursday (Sept. 18, 2025) shares on his social media account his dinner  — okra given to him by a young boy named “Batching,” whom he met earlier at the evacuation center for fire victims in Happy Land, Tondo, Manila.

“Thank you for my dinner tonight, Batching ❤️🙏🏽,” the President wrote in his post.

Earlier in the day, Marcos visited General Vicente Lim Elementary School to lead the distribution of relief goods and cash assistance to more than 2,000 families affected by the massive fire. | via Darryl Esguerra (📸 Bongbong Marcos Facebook)
